answer: Divergent-Challenge Window. Each identity must answer fresh randomized challenges within a latency bound; genuine agents diverge cheaply, but a cloned fleet shares one decision trace, so answers collide. Responses are hashed into an atlas of per-identity traces, and any collision across supposedly independent identities voids all involved. The rule is hollow only on paper: an attacker must run each clone on separate hardware with independent context, paying full per-identity compute and coordination cost rather than one opal copy broadcast to thousands.
